CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for rash management.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting for follow-up of perioral dermatitis/rosacea. She reports her condition is doing much better. Initially treated with doxycycline twice daily with significant improvement noted over the first two weeks. One week ago, patient reduced doxycycline to once daily on pharmacist recommendation, but notes improvement has plateaued. Patient reports small amount of rash still present. She confirms she is no longer breastfeeding and discontinued breastfeeding prior to starting doxycycline. Patient previously avoided Elidel cream after reading about potential risks but was counseled by provider regarding the safety profile of topical formulations.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Skin: Persistent small rash on face, sun sensitivity. Patient reports taking sun precautions including wearing hat when outdoors. Denies dryness of face. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, ocular rosacea.

MEDICATIONS
Doxycycline (to be increased to twice daily), sulfacetamide wash (twice daily), metronidazole cream (applied after face wash), tacrolimus ointment (newly prescribed), vanicream moisturizer or petroleum jelly (samples provided).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not breastfeeding. Takes sun protection precautions including wearing hat.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV. Bilateral medial cheeks with faint erythematous papules. Mild erythema around and underneath nostrils. No other significant findings.

RESULTS
Physical examination as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. Plan: (1) Continue sulfacetamide face wash, consider reducing to once daily if drying occurs; (2) Continue metronidazole cream; (3) Increase doxycycline to twice daily until rash resolves, then continue once daily for one additional week before discontinuing; (4) Add tacrolimus ointment (calcineurin inhibitor) applied to affected areas twice daily until resolved—patient counseled regarding temporary tingly or flushing sensation that may occur; (5) Add gentle moisturizer (vanicream or petroleum jelly); samples provided; (6) Gently wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream; use Bruder mask as needed; (7) Avoid steroids and new skincare products; discuss any new products with provider prior to use; (8) Cancel Elidel cream and clindamycin from medication list; (9) Follow-up appointment in approximately 4 weeks; (10) Contact provider via phone or MyChart if rash worsens or fails to improve.
